newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. cancels more Colombians' travel visas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cancels more Colombians' travel visas.

text.p: The United States cancelled the U.S. travel visas of dozens of Colombians this week because they were believed to be acting as fronts for the Cali drug cartel, the American embassy in Bogota announced.
Forty-six names were added on Thursday to the U.S. Treasury Department's list of Specially Designated Narcotics Traffickers in Colombia.
A terse embassy statement said anyone who appears on the list is automatically stripped of his or her U.S. visa by the State Department.
People wishing to reapply could do so, the statement added, saying eligibility for entry to the United States was open to review on a case-by-case basis.
Embassy officials could not be reached for details on how many Colombians had their visas cancelled in the past year.

The numbers include President Ernesto Samper, whose U.S. travel rights were revoked in July 1996 amid the scandal over accusations that he used Cali cartel drug money to finance his election campaign.
